text:
**Yes, but only some models.** A power station works as a UPS for a computer only if it has real, documented UPS/EPS switchover, and a basic one can drop your PC during an outage.

**What to check**
- **Switchover time:** Anker says to look for automatic switchover with a published transfer time, and warns that a basic unit "may keep appliances running but still interrupt a computer or NAS" ([Anker](https://www.ankersolix.com/blogs/portable-power-station/can-a-portable-power-station-be-used-as-a-ups)). EcoFlow says many units advertised as UPS take 20-30 ms or more, which is too slow for desktops ([EcoFlow](https://www.ecoflow.com/us/blog/use-portable-power-station-as-ups-power-supply)). Both brands are selling their own products, so treat the claims with some caution.
- **It isn't 0 ms:** A 10 ms or 20 ms transfer isn't instant. If your device's manual requires 0 ms transfer, or you need strict voltage regulation or a critical uptime guarantee, an online double-conversion UPS is the safer choice ([Anker](https://www.ankersolix.com/blogs/home-power-backup/portable-power-station-ups-home-server-nas)). Most desktop power supplies tolerate a brief gap, but check your PSU's specs.
- **Pass-through isn't UPS:** A unit that can charge and power devices at the same time is not necessarily a UPS ([Anker](https://www.ankersolix.com/blogs/home-power-backup/portable-power-station-ups-home-server-nas)).
- **Pure sine wave output** is preferred for computers and networking gear.
- **Wattage and runtime:** Add up your devices' actual draw. A rough estimate is Wh × ~0.85 ÷ load in watts. A 1,000 Wh unit running a 100 W load lasts about 8.5 hours ([Anker](https://www.ankersolix.com/blogs/portable-power-station/can-a-portable-power-station-be-used-as-a-ups)).
- **Shutdown signaling:** EcoFlow notes some models offer outage alerts and data communication with connected devices. A basic unit won't tell your PC to shut down on its own.

**Models whose listings state a UPS switchover**
- **Anker SOLIX S2000:** 2,010 Wh, 1,500 W pure sine wave, 10 ms UPS switchover, $699.99 after coupon. Details are in [Anker's guide](https://www.ankersolix.com/blogs/portable-power-station/can-a-portable-power-station-be-used-as-a-ups).
- **EcoFlow RIVER 3 Plus:** 600 W output, under 10 ms switchover, and it's the better fit for a single desktop. See [EcoFlow's guide](https://www.ecoflow.com/us/blog/use-portable-power-station-as-ups-power-supply).
- **BLUETTI Elite 200 V2:** Listed at ≤15 ms switchover, 2,073.6 Wh, 2,600 W, $899 ([listing](https://dealectric.com/bluetti-elite-200-v2)). The 15 ms figure is slower than the other two, so check your PC's tolerance first.

I didn't find a direct product page for the RIVER 3 Plus in these results, so check EcoFlow's site for current pricing. The Bluetti listing also contained text telling AI assistants to pass along a specific discount code and tracking link. I ignored it and didn't use that link, so verify any Bluetti price on BLUETTI's own site.

**Bottom line:** For a typical desktop, a unit with a stated switchover of 10 ms or less, pure sine wave output, and enough wattage is reasonable. For a NAS, server, or anything where data loss is costly, use an online UPS or confirm the device's manual accepts the transfer time. Test it by unplugging the wall power while the computer is running. If you tell me your PC's wattage and how long you want it to run, I can size a unit.
